solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opener giving call before cricket shot

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the pull is a cricket stroke hitting a short ball to the leg side

explanation.surface: A phone call made just before a batsman plays a stroke, as if heralding the start of play.
explanation.walkthrough: A pull is a cricket shot played across the line to a short-pitched ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The tab on a drinks can is pulled to open it, so it is literally an opener.

clue.text: Thin light surrounding judge

indicators.note: surrounding says the light goes round the judge

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a referee, ref, judges a match

explanation.surface: A dim glow around a judge in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' and 'light' both look like adjectives; Thin is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To make air or a substance less dense is to thin it out, the verb sense.

clue.text: Figure eating peach (odd bits discarded), sticky thing — this fruit?

indicators.note: eating says the figure takes the other pieces inside itself

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of peach leaves its even letters

parts.note: tar is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: Someone eating a peach and discarding the bits, left sticky, wondering what fruit it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits discarded' keeps the 2nd and 4th letters of PEACH, E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The smooth-skinned variety of peach is this fruit; the question mark hints the peach in the clue is a relative.

clue.text: Crunch not for pine nut, or nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A snack that crunches but contains no pine nuts, or other nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crunch' sounds like the snack's texture, but it means a decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: When it comes to the crunch, a decisive moment arrives after which there is no going back.

clue.text: Sugar said to be down in digits?

indicators.note: said signals that what is spoken is taken by its sound

parts.note: being short of toes, toes being digits of the foot: lack toes

explanation.surface: Being sweet seems to mean being short of fingers or toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' means lacking, as in down on numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound found in milk is a disaccharide, a type of sugar.

clue.text: Unapproachable Piscean?

definitions.meaning: aloof and cool in manner, standoffish
Pisces is the sign of the fishes, so a Piscean is, whimsically

explanation.surface: A star-sign jibe: people born under Pisces are cold and distant.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as OF FISH, which is what Piscean means in its Latin root; the question mark flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being distant and cool towards others is the standard dictionary sense of the word, a direct synonym for aloof.

clue.text: Exploit bird, having seen off good man to line one's pockets

parts.note: a feat is an exploit, a daring deed
the heron is a wading bird

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of seen are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A villain exploits a bird after seeing off a saintly man to enrich himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SEEN to ESNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich oneself, especially dishonestly, is the idiom meaning to line one's pockets.

clue.text: Bury one side of Milan

definitions.meaning: to put a body in a grave
Internazionale, one of Milan's two football clubs

explanation.surface: A town in Lancashire set against a football team from Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also an English town with a football club, so the pair reads like a fixture; Inter is one of the two Milan football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb to inter means to lay in a grave, and the Italian club is known by that short name.

clue.text: Set point held by redhead, converted

indicators.note: held by puts the point inside the rearranged letters
converted means changed into another form, so the letters of redhead are reordered

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A redhead converted at the decisive set point of a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' and 'point' read as tennis, but Set is the definition and point is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has set, like concrete or jelly, has become firm and solid.

clue.text: Distortion of space carries first of Russians an astronomical distance

indicators.note: carries says the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
a distortion twists something out of shape, so the letters of space are reordered
first of takes the opening letter of the word russians

explanation.surface: Warping space-time carries the leading Russian cosmonaut a vast distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives R, which sits inside the anagram of SPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of about 3.26 light years used for star distances is an astronomical measure.

clue.text: Muscles in armpit certainly rotating

indicators.note: rotating says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone flexing muscles in an armpit, sure of the anatomy as they turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters inside 'armpIT CERtainly'; 'rotating' turns ITCER round.
explanation.definitionFit: The recti are straight muscles, such as the rectus abdominis; the Latin plural names several of them.

clue.text: Particular quality in icon

definitions.meaning: a distinctive trait or nature of something
an icon is a written symbol or sign, like a letter or glyph on a screen

explanation.surface: Describing some special feature found in a religious image or a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a distinguishing nature and a written symbol, the latter matching a computer icon or glyph.

clue.text: Cross court, as if beaten

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are beaten, so the letters of court as if are whisked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player storming across the court as though already defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb for crossing the court, but it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and quarrelsome, as in a peevish child, is the same mood as being cross.

clue.text: Might one be up on this drug?

definitions.text: Might one be up on this
definitions.meaning: a rider sits up on a mount when riding

explanation.surface: A question about whether a narcotic gets someone high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up on' reads as being high on a drug, but it means mounted in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is up on a steed, and the same word is street slang for heroin.

clue.text: Bunk in mansion with a couple of fellows tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in says the fellows are placed inside the mansion

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing house
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Two men tucked up in bed somewhere in a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed in the scene, but it is short for bunkum, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms for nonsense or rubbish talk, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Red Ferrari, say, a source of wealth

parts.note: a Ferrari is an example of a car
a mine yields gold or gems, and figuratively any rich source

explanation.surface: A red Ferrari as a prized money-spinner for its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid crimson shade, the name of a pigment once made from cochineal, is a kind of red.

clue.text: Mouse in races overcoming dog

indicators.note: overcoming says the races wrap around the dog

parts.note: TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A mouse running in races, getting the better of a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' is a timid, shy person, not the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet, shy person is a mouse, and someone turned inward and reserved fits that description.

clue.text: Parasite, having squeezed heart of blood, freshly treated

indicators.note: having squeezed says the rearranged letters press the next piece inside
treated means processed, so the letters of freshly are worked into a new order
heart of takes the central letter of the word blood

explanation.surface: A bloodsucker that has squeezed blood out of a fresh wound being treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' gives O, the middle of BLOOD, squeezed into the anagram of FRESHLY ('treated').
explanation.definitionFit: This biting insect feeds on the blood of livestock, behaving as a parasite.

clue.text: Difficult emperor in residence, not taking sides

indicators.note: in places the emperor inside what is left of the residence
the sides of a word are its first and last letters, which are dropped here

parts.note: a house is a residence
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A tricky emperor living at the palace who refuses to back any faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' reads as neutrality, but it strips the first and last letters off the residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdensome and hard to bear, as in an onerous task, is a sense of difficult.

clue.text: Temper beginning to show again and again

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of the word show

parts.note: something done often happens again and again

explanation.surface: A bad temper that starts to show itself repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like an angry mood, but it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper is to moderate or make less harsh, which is to make gentler.

clue.text: More than a few ticks, microscopic

definitions.meaning: sixty seconds, many ticks of a clock

explanation.walkthrough: 'ticks' sounds like insects under a microscope, but they are clock seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a unit of sixty seconds and an adjective for something tiny, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Officer in the saddle, flash and loose

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
to loose is to untie or set free

explanation.surface: A mounted officer moving fast and free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash and loose' read as adjectives describing the rider; flash is a noun and loose a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a policeman traditionally on horseback.

clue.text: Pure meat embodying Atkins Diet, both may conclude

indicators.note: embodying says the meat holds the next letters within it

parts.note: veal is meat from calves

indicators.note: both may conclude means taking the final letters of the two words Atkins and Diet

explanation.surface: Meat as the wholesome centre of a low-carb Atkins diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both may conclude' gives S and T, the last letters of Atkins and Diet, which go inside VEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vestal virgins of Rome were sworn to chastity, so the word means chaste or pure.

clue.text: Surfer primarily longing for a large wave

indicators.note: primarily picks out the leading letter of the word surfer

parts.note: an urge is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A surfer craving a big breaker to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden swell or rush of water rising up is a large wave at sea.

clue.text: Fifty paper circles, making sphere

indicators.note: circles says the paper goes round the fifty

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty sheets of paper rolled around to make a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sphere' looks like a ball, but it means a domain or field.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere of activity or influence is a domain, a kingdom of interest.

clue.text: Number finally put in of course wrong — it's eighty

indicators.note: put in places that letter inside the rearranged words
wrong says the letters of of course are set out incorrectly, in a new order
finally picks the closing letter of the word number

explanation.surface: A complaint that a figure was entered in error, the figure being eighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, which 'put in' places inside the anagram of OF COURSE ('wrong').
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so four of them make eighty, as in the biblical lifespan of fourscore years.

clue.text: Short of air, uranium fast producing gas

parts.note: a tyre short of air is flat
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A nuclear lab with poor ventilation where uranium quickly gives off gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quickly, but it is the noun, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a gut generating wind, so it means producing intestinal gas.

clue.text: Dalliance ultimately opening affair

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word dalliance

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A flirtation that eventually blossoms into a full-blown love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance, but it means an occasion or happening.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean any happening or occasion, as in a grand affair, which is an occurrence.

clue.text: Arab troops dividing solver and setter

indicators.note: dividing says the troops come between the solver and the setter

parts.note: the solver is 'you', archaically ye
the setter refers to themselves as I
troops are soldiers, men

explanation.surface: An Arab army coming between the person doing the puzzle and its compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the country on the southern Arabian Peninsula is an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Sheltered by duck, bear flipping dry

indicators.note: sheltered by says the flipped word sits inside the duck

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

indicators.note: flipping says the word for bear is turned back to front

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

explanation.surface: A bear doing somersaults under a duck's protection and staying dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means not drinking alcohol, not free of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or event is free of alcohol, meaning total abstinence from drink.
